question: On development prefixes admitted by the unchanged baseline rule, does a prefix-only fit preference (gravity-only line vs OLS line, equal parameters) separate groups whose short-horizon forecasts behave differently, and how do persistence, OLS velocity and gravity-only continuation compare within each group at 50/100/200 ms? Prefix-only use of supplied (possibly processed) tracks; no causal-pipeline or physical-accuracy claim.

not_opened.P0004: historically consulted validation participant; the task card allows one consultation only after this development decision is frozen, which is NOT part of this packet

indicator.meaning: gravity preferred over the line on this prefix: fit_gravity_ballistic_segment RMSE strictly below the OLS constant-velocity RMSE, both 6 parameters, 3-D RMSE over exactly the finite prefix samples fit_prefix admits; ties are not gravity_consistent
indicator.not_a: release label, contact/no-contact classification, or certification of ideal-gravity physics: for noise-free vertical acceleration a the preference holds whenever a < -g/2 (about -4.905 m/s^2)

candidates.persistence: unchanged OW-PREFIX-07: last admitted prefix observation
candidates.velocity: unchanged OW-PREFIX-07: OLS intercept at the cutoff plus velocity times (target time - cutoff)
candidates.gravity: fit_gravity_ballistic_segment on the admitted prefix samples, predicted at the native target time; role 'mismatched_comparator' in the not_gravity_consistent group, 'candidate' otherwise

freeze: per-trial prefix fits, indicator, native target times and all predictions are written to frozen_predictions.json and hashed before any reference position is read for scoring; the hash is re-checked after scoring

retrospective_agreement.mapping: future_gravity_preferred if OW-REGIME-17 rmse_gravity_m < rmse_constant_velocity_m; future_line_preferred if both present and not smaller; future_undefined if either is missing
retrospective_agreement.label: prefix-versus-future fit-preference agreement (retrospective diagnostic; never used to choose predictions, groups, thresholds or cutoffs)

metrics: 3-D Euclidean error (m) against the first native target at or after each horizon; mean, median, p90 and n by participant/session x indicator x horizon x candidate, and overall by indicator; per-trial paired differences velocity-persistence, gravity-velocity, gravity-persistence; requested and actual target time retained; empty groups are undefined (null), never zero
examples: deterministic: for each participant/session x indicator with n>0, the trial with the median 200 ms velocity error (representative) and the one with the maximum 200 ms velocity error (failure), ties broken by path
